summary.method: Rule-based classifier (classify.py) over title, head branch, first 700 chars of body and changed-file paths (merged: GitHub REST pulls/files; closed: pr-files export), then 72 per-PR overrides after reviewing every non-controller PR title. Controller detection: title prefixes (TEMP/Never merge/Controller/CONSUMED/SUPERSEDED/FAILED...), body markers (execution-only, disposable, never merge, transport-only), >=50% carrier files (.github/temporary, .github/tmp, dot-dirs) or PR #2231 qualifier titles. Spot check: a 50-PR random sample of the controller class contained no non-controller PRs; all ~700 non-controller PRs were read by title. Category boundaries (e.g. PC lab = self-checking, topology admissions = findings, receipt-store hardening = self-checking) are judgement calls; see effort_split.sensitivity.
summary.provenance_caveat: Every PR, issue and comment in the export is posted through the BigBirdReturns account (1,528 of 2,536 comments; PR authors are not in the export). Agent sessions and the owner share that identity, so no verbatim human-typed text can be separated. The "owner_directives" below are the programme-defining or decision-recording texts (agent-written, relaying owner instructions) plus BUILD-INSTRUCTIONS.md, which is the only document written in an author's own voice. Treat them as instructions of record, not as verbatim prompts.

all_topics.topic: Machinery: scheduled-crawler admission, App identity, main protection

definition.a_real_world: touching the real world = research_acquisition + analysis_findings + case_brief (sources, findings, briefs)
definition.c_checking_themselves: checking themselves = validators_selftests + governance_docs (validators, tests, synthetic-control labs, constitution, ledgers, milestones)
definition.d_moving_own_work_around: moving their own work around = controller_dispatch + cleanup_retirement + ci_workflow

effort_split.file_basis_note: Files are counted per PR from GitHub file lists (merged: fetched via REST pulls/files, 14,092 files; closed/open: pr-files export, 8,319 files; 4 PRs capped at 500). Controller files inflate the (d) file share because each payload is chunked into many one-line base64 parts; PR counts are the primary measure.
effort_split.plain_answer: By PR count roughly 16% of the agents' effort touched the real world (sources, findings, briefs), 5% built tools/the site, 10% checked themselves, and 69% moved their own work around (66% controller/TEMP/never-merge PRs alone). Of the 30% of PRs that actually landed on main it is 46% real world, 11% tools/site, 30% self-checking and 13% plumbing/cleanup. Two windows (Aug 1-11 and Aug 26-Sep 2) hold 1,523 PRs (74% of all PRs) and are 80% controller PRs.

controllers_by_what_they_served.note: Controller PRs are scored by form (disposable CI-driven carriers), not by payload; most real-world programmes ran their fetches/adjudications inside them.

controllers_that_were_themselves_externa.note: Some TEMP PRs ARE the run that fetched official sources (e.g. "TEMP: capture School.House state-registry candidates", "TEMP: execute exact RD-04 postpromotion five-route capture"). Regex estimate only.

c_if_PC_lab_validators_were_instead_coun.note: PC lab validators are all synthetic fixtures; no real-world effect declared

d_range.note: low end reclassifies every controller whose title says capture/probe/crawl/census/discover/acquire/redirect as real-world work

programme_purpose_lens.note: Second lens: group PRs by the purpose of the programme (topic) they belong to rather than by what the PR itself does. Real-world programmes absorb most PRs, but only a minority of their PRs are the acquisition/finding/brief itself.
